narrative.northStar: I-95 at Dusk, Driven by Your Scroll
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "I-95 at Dusk, Driven by Your Scroll"**

The page opens from the driver's seat: a dusk sky going peach at the horizon, a pine treeline, a two-lane road with white edge lines and yellow center dashes (one right in front of the camera) bending gently right, reflector posts on both shoulders and a green I-95 guide sign just ahead. Over it, in huge uppercase white, "You fly, / I'll drive.", the second line in lane yellow. The road runs behind the whole page, and only the reader moves it: scrolling down backs the camera away so the road, posts and sign recede toward the horizon; scrolling up brings them back. Every section after the hero is an overhead road sign on a real steel structure (Meet your driver on a cantilever from the right, the $1-a-mile form on a span truss, Straight answers as a stack of small plates on a roadside post), and the solid deep-green footer is where the road ends, closing with the call.

Density is low and type is big for a 40-to-70 reader on a phone. The ground is deep roadside green, never black. Lane yellow is the action color; a sky-blue outline is the one hover/focus voice. Nothing moves on its own.
keyCharacteristics: A fixed canvas road at dusk behind the whole page, driven only by the reader's scroll; still under reduced motion.
An uppercase two-line headline and one yellow "Get a rate by text" button; the header number is the call action.

Every section is a guide-sign panel (green, inset white rule, 16px corners) hung on a real steel structure (cantilever from the right, span truss, cantilever from the left); once it climbs past the road it shrinks toward the horizon.
One yellow for action; one sky-blue outline for hover and focus; shamrock green only for the footer call.
One system font stack worked by weight: 900 headings, 800 controls, 400 talk.
Phone-first, big targets (48px links, 58 to 76px controls), 17px text floor.

rules.name: The Never-Black Rule
rules.body: The darkest surface is ground-deep. Black appears only inside soft shadows, never as a ground.

rules.name: The One Yellow Rule
rules.body: In the interface, a yellow rectangle is always a control. Yellow type is reserved for the headline's second line, the price, links and icons. The road picture paints yellow where a real road has it (center dashes, left reflectors).

rules.name: The One Outline Rule
rules.body: Hover and focus on every control is a 3px focus-sky outline (offset 2 to 3px; 6px radius on text links). No other hover color, fill change or glow.

rules.name: The 65 MPH Rule
rules.body: No text under 17px (the narrow-phone wordmark is the single exception), and nothing a reader acts on is lighter than 700.

rules.name: The Reader Drives Rule
rules.body: Motion comes only from the reader's own scroll; nothing is ever autonomous. Scrolling down backs the camera away (travel falls) so the dashes, posts and the I-95 sign recede toward the horizon; scrolling up brings them back. The camera scale is fixed at its top-of-page value, so the road slides up and never zooms. Once a sign's foot rises above 30% of the road height it shrinks toward the horizon along the road (scale from its bottom center, translate along the road, fading out between scale 0.42 and 0.12). The canvas redraws once per scroll frame and on a real resize, nothing more: no loop, no autoplay, no entrance effects. Control transitions: button press (translateY 1px, scale .99 over .2s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)), outline color (.15s), trip-row color (.15s). The jump to the form scrolls smoothly. Under prefers-reduced-motion the road is one still frame, signs never transform, the jump is instant and transitions are off.

rules.name: The Mounted Sign Rule
rules.body: The only raised surfaces are the sign panels and the call buttons. Content on a sign stays flat, divided by space or rules, never cards inside the sign.

dos: Do let only the reader's scroll move the road and the signs; keep it a still frame under reduced motion.
Do keep the hero to the two-line uppercase headline, the promise, and one yellow button to the form; the call lives in the header.
Do hang every section after the hero on a real structure (cantilever or span truss), alternating sides down the page, never floating on bare posts.
Do use the 3px focus-sky outline for every hover and focus.
Do keep controls 58px or taller, links 48px, answer choices as large rows, text at 17px or larger.
Do show answers in full; a question and its answer sit together.
donts: Don't animate anything on its own: no drive loop, autoplay, timed reveals or entrance effects; no zoom on scroll.
Don't use accordions, tabs, carousels or other hide-and-reveal patterns.
Don't use black or neutral charcoal as any ground; the darkest is ground-deep.
Don't add a sticky header or sticky call bar, or email links.
Don't add a second hero action; the call is the header number.
Don't put yellow fills on interface non-controls.
Don't use hard offset shadows; depth is soft.
